result.paraphrase: Object-sensitivity is a common context abstraction for computing context-sensitive points-to information in object-oriented languages such as Java. Because the number of contexts grows combinatorially in large programs, k-object-sensitive pointer analysis (under k-limiting), denoted k-obj, scales only for small k values, typically k ⩽ 2. Some recent approaches try to speed it up by having k-obj analyze only selected methods context-sensitively, with the selection determined heuristically by a pre-analysis. Although effective, these heuristic pre-analyses offer no precision guarantees and therefore provide only limited efficiency gains. We present a fundamentally different approach, Eagle, which makes k-obj run much faster than prior methods while preserving its precision. Eagle’s key idea is to let k-obj analyze a method with partial context-sensitivity, meaning context-sensitively for only some chosen variables or allocation sites. These selections are made during a lightweight pre-analysis that reasons about context-free-language (CFL) reachability at the level of program variables and objects, using a new CFL-reachability formulation of k-obj. We show Eagle’s improvements by comparing it with prior art on a set of popular Java benchmarks and applications.
